title: General Biology I
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 100L General Biology I curriculum: characteristics and classification of living organisms, cell structure and function, biomolecules, cell division, enzymes, genetics fundamentals, and introductory ecology.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the generally accepted characteristics of living organisms?
questions.explanation: Crystallization is a physical process seen in non-living matter; it is not a characteristic used to define living organisms, unlike reproduction, irritability, and metabolism.

questions.question: The ability of an organism to maintain a stable internal environment despite external changes is called:
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the regulatory process by which living organisms keep internal conditions such as temperature and pH relatively constant.

questions.question: The scientific naming system that gives every organism a two-part Latin name (genus and species) is called:
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature, developed by Carl Linnaeus, assigns each species a two-part name consisting of its genus and species epithet.

questions.question: Arrange the following taxonomic ranks from broadest to narrowest: Class, Genus, Kingdom, Order, Species, Phylum, Family.
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Order, Family, Species, Genus
Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.correct_answer: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The standard taxonomic hierarchy from broadest to most specific is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: The five-kingdom system of classification, proposed by Whittaker, includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and:
questions.explanation: Whittaker's five-kingdom classification comprises Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

questions.question: Organisms in the Kingdom Monera are characterized by:
options: having prokaryotic cells with no true nucleus
having eukaryotic cells with membrane-bound organelles
questions.correct_answer: having prokaryotic cells with no true nucleus
questions.explanation: Monerans (bacteria) are prokaryotes; their genetic material is not enclosed within a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.question: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
questions.explanation: Cell theory states that the cell is the smallest unit that carries out all the functions necessary for life.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus while prokaryotic cells do not
Prokaryotic cells have mitochondria while eukaryotic cells do not
Eukaryotic cells lack a cell membrane
Prokaryotic cells are always larger than eukaryotic cells
questions.correct_answer: Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus while prokaryotic cells do not
questions.explanation: The defining distinction between the two cell types is the presence (eukaryotes) or absence (prokaryotes) of a true, membrane-enclosed nucleus.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is responsible for producing most of the ATP used by the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, generating the bulk of a cell's ATP, earning them the name 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.question: The organelle responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells is the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site where light energy is converted into chemical energy during photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which structure controls the passage of substances into and out of the cell?
questions.explanation: The selectively permeable plasma membrane regulates what enters and leaves the cell.

questions.question: A structural feature found in plant cells but not in animal cells is the:
questions.explanation: Plant cells possess a rigid cellulose cell wall external to the plasma membrane, which animal cells lack.

questions.question: Ribosomes are the cell organelles responsible for:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains, making them the site of protein synthesis.

questions.question: The organelle that modifies, packages, and ships proteins and lipids is the:
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus processes proteins and lipids received from the endoplasmic reticulum and packages them for transport or secretion.

questions.question: Lysosomes are important in the cell mainly because they:
options: contain digestive enzymes that break down waste materials and worn-out organelles
questions.correct_answer: contain digestive enzymes that break down waste materials and worn-out organelles
questions.explanation: Lysosomes house hydrolytic enzymes used to digest macromolecules, foreign particles, and damaged organelles.

questions.question: Movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration is called:
questions.explanation: Osmosis is specifically the diffusion of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane along its concentration gradient.

questions.question: The movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration without the use of cellular energy is:
questions.explanation: Diffusion is a passive process driven by the concentration gradient and requires no direct expenditure of ATP.

questions.question: Movement of substances against their concentration gradient, requiring energy, is called:
questions.explanation: Active transport moves molecules from low to high concentration and therefore requires ATP to work against the natural gradient.

questions.question: The four major classes of biomolecules essential to living organisms are carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and:
questions.explanation: The four major biomolecule classes are carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

questions.question: The building blocks (monomers) of proteins are:
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers built from chains of amino acids linked together by peptide bonds.

questions.question: The bond that links amino acids together in a protein chain is called a:
questions.explanation: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next.

questions.question: Carbohydrates are composed of the elements:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are made up of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, typically in a ratio close to 1:2:1.

questions.question: Glucose, fructose, and galactose are all examples of:
questions.explanation: Glucose, fructose, and galactose are simple sugars (monosaccharides) that cannot be broken down into smaller sugar units.

questions.question: The main storage polysaccharide of carbohydrates in plants is:
questions.explanation: Plants store excess glucose as starch, whereas glycogen is the storage form of glucose in animals.

questions.question: The genetic material of most living organisms is:
questions.explanation: DNA carries the hereditary genetic instructions in nearly all living organisms, with RNA playing a genetic role only in certain viruses.

questions.question: A nucleotide is composed of a nitrogenous base, a sugar, and a:
questions.explanation: Each nucleotide consists of a five-carbon sugar, a nitrogenous base, and one or more phosphate groups.

questions.question: In DNA, adenine always pairs with:
questions.explanation: DNA base pairing follows complementary rules: adenine pairs with thymine, and guanine pairs with cytosine.

questions.question: Enzymes are best described as:
options: Biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed
Structural proteins that form the cytoskeleton
Lipids that make up cell membranes
questions.correct_answer: Biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins (with a few RNA exceptions) that lower the activation energy of reactions and are not used up in the process.

questions.question: The specific region of an enzyme where the substrate binds is called the:
questions.explanation: The active site is the enzyme's specialized region that binds the substrate and catalyzes the reaction.

questions.question: Which factor generally increases enzyme activity up to an optimum point, beyond which the enzyme becomes denatured?
questions.explanation: Enzyme activity rises with temperature up to an optimum; beyond that point, the rise in temperature denatures the enzyme's structure and activity falls sharply.

questions.question: A substance that reduces enzyme activity by binding to the enzyme is called a(n):
questions.explanation: Inhibitors bind to enzymes (at the active site or elsewhere) and reduce or block their catalytic activity.

questions.question: The type of cell division that produces two genetically identical daughter cells for growth and repair is:
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two daughter cells genetically identical to the parent cell and is used for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction.

questions.question: Meiosis differs from mitosis in that meiosis:
options: produces four genetically varied daughter cells with half the chromosome number
produces two identical diploid daughter cells
questions.correct_answer: produces four genetically varied daughter cells with half the chromosome number
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two successive divisions that halve the chromosome number and introduce genetic variation, producing gametes.

questions.question: During which phase of mitosis do chromosomes align at the cell's equator (metaphase plate)?
questions.explanation: In metaphase, chromosomes line up along the cell's equatorial plane, attached to spindle fibres from opposite poles.

questions.question: During anaphase of mitosis, the:
options: sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
chromosomes first condense and become visible
nuclear membrane reforms around the chromosomes
questions.correct_answer: sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
questions.explanation: Anaphase is marked by the separation of sister chromatids, which are then pulled to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.question: The process by which the cytoplasm divides to form two separate daughter cells after nuclear division is called:
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm that physically separates the two daughter cells following nuclear division.

questions.question: In genetics, an allele that is expressed in the phenotype whenever it is present, masking the other allele, is called:
questions.explanation: A dominant allele's trait shows up in the phenotype even in the presence of a different (recessive) allele.

questions.question: An organism with two identical alleles for a given gene (e.g. TT or tt) is said to be:
questions.explanation: Homozygous describes an organism carrying two identical alleles of a gene, in contrast to heterozygous, which carries two different alleles.

questions.question: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous (Tt x Tt) parents, the expected phenotypic ratio in the offspring is:
questions.explanation: Mendel's monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes yields a classic 3:1 phenotypic ratio of dominant to recessive traits.

questions.question: An organism's observable physical or biochemical characteristics constitute its:
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable traits of an organism resulting from the interaction of its genotype with the environment.

questions.question: The genetic constitution of an organism, in terms of the alleles it carries, is called its:
questions.explanation: Genotype is the specific allelic makeup of an organism for a given trait or across its genome.

questions.question: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that:
options: the two alleles for a trait separate during gamete formation, so each gamete carries only one allele
genes for different traits are always inherited together
dominant alleles are always more common in a population
alleles blend together to form an intermediate phenotype
questions.correct_answer: the two alleles for a trait separate during gamete formation, so each gamete carries only one allele
questions.explanation: The Law of Segregation explains that paired alleles separate during meiosis so that each gamete receives only one allele of each gene.

questions.question: A group of similar cells performing a specific function together forms a:
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of structurally similar cells that work together to perform a shared function.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly shows the levels of biological organization from simplest to most complex?
options: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
Organism, organ, tissue, cell, organ system
Tissue, cell, organ system, organ, organism
Organ, tissue, cell, organism, organ system
questions.correct_answer: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
questions.explanation: Biological organization proceeds from cells, which form tissues, which form organs, which form organ systems, which together make up the whole organism.

questions.question: Meristematic tissue in plants is significant because it:
options: consists of actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth
transports water and minerals throughout the plant
stores food reserves in the roots
protects the plant from water loss
questions.correct_answer: consists of actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth
questions.explanation: Meristematic tissue is composed of undifferentiated cells that continually divide by mitosis, enabling plant growth at root and shoot tips.

questions.question: In ecology, all the living organisms of one species occupying a given area at the same time make up a:
questions.explanation: A population consists of all individuals of a single species living together in a specific area.

questions.question: A community together with its non-living (abiotic) environment forms a(n):
questions.explanation: An ecosystem is the interacting system of a biological community and its physical, non-living environment.

questions.question: Organisms that manufacture their own food from inorganic substances, such as green plants, are called:
questions.explanation: Autotrophs, mainly green plants and some bacteria, synthesize their own organic food using light or chemical energy, forming the base of most food chains.

questions.question: Organisms that break down dead organic matter and recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem are called:
questions.explanation: Decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, break down dead organisms and waste, releasing nutrients back into the environment.

questions.question: The sequence showing how energy and nutrients pass from one organism to another through feeding is called a:
questions.explanation: A food chain represents the linear transfer of energy from producers through a series of consumers.

questions.question: The theory that explains how species change over time through natural selection was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in 'On the Origin of Species'.

questions.question: Natural selection acts on a population mainly through:
options: differential survival and reproduction of individuals with favourable traits
random mutation alone, with no effect of environment
deliberate selection by organisms of their own traits
the equal survival of all individuals regardless of traits
questions.correct_answer: differential survival and reproduction of individuals with favourable traits
questions.explanation: Natural selection favours individuals whose heritable traits improve survival and reproductive success, so those traits become more common over generations.

questions.question: Who is credited with first observing and naming 'cells' using a microscope while examining cork tissue?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke first used the term 'cell' in 1665 after observing the compartments in cork tissue under a microscope.

questions.question: According to the cell theory, which statement is TRUE?
options: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells
Only animals are made up of cells
Cells can arise spontaneously from non-living matter
All cells in an organism are identical in structure
questions.correct_answer: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells
questions.explanation: A core tenet of cell theory is that all living things are made up of one or more cells, and cells arise only from pre-existing cells.
